tip: Bypass (B): hear the dry signal, delayed to match, to compare with the shaped sound. The meters keep moving.
Number of bands: 1 to 4. Each band shapes its own part of the sound. Drag the vertical dividers in the graph to place the crossovers. Unused bands are greyed out.
Crossover slope: how steeply the bands are separated, from 12 to 96 dB per octave. Default 24. Steeper keeps bands cleaner but rings a little more. The bands always add back flat.
Crossover 1: where band 1 ends and band 2 starts.
Crossover 2: where band 2 ends and band 3 starts.
Crossover 3: where band 3 ends and band 4 starts.
Input gain in dB, before everything else. The shaper reacts to level changes, not to the absolute level, so this mainly sets how hard the threshold and the limiter are hit. Double-click for 0.
Output gain in dB, after the Mix and before the limiter, so you can push the sound into the limiter. Double-click for 0.
Mix: shaped sound against the untouched input (delayed to match, so there is no comb filtering). 100% is fully shaped, 0% is exactly the input.
Limiter on or off. A lookahead limiter at the very end: nothing leaves the plugin above the Ceiling, whatever the Mix.
Limiter ceiling in dB, -12 to 0. Nothing leaves the plugin above this level. Default -0.3.
Auto release: the limiter lets go slowly after a hard hit and quickly after a light one. Switch it off to set the release by hand.
Limiter release in ms: how fast the limiter lets go after a peak. Used when Auto is off. 5 to 500 ms.
Lookahead in ms, 1 to 7.5 (default 3). The limiter sees peaks this long before they play, so it can turn down smoothly. Longer is cleaner, shorter is lower latency. It sets the reported latency.
Listen: hear the result (All), only the attack part (Transients) or only the sustain part (Sustain). The two parts add up to the shaped sound. Handy for setting a band by ear.

Boost: makes Attack and Sustain act harder, for extreme shaping. x1 is the normal range (default), x2 doubles and x4 quadruples how many dB each percent can add or take away. Raise a band Max dB to let it go further. The limiter at the end still keeps the output under the Ceiling.
Spectrum behind the bands. In + Out shows the input in grey and the output in green. The scale on the right is dBFS.
Band 1: power. Off lets the band pass untouched (it still goes through the crossover).
Mute this band: its sound is removed from the output.
Solo this band: hear only soloed bands.
Band 1: Attack. Plus makes the first hit of each sound louder (more snap and punch). Minus softens it. 0 leaves it alone. Double-click for 0.
Band 1: Sustain. Plus makes what comes after the hit louder (longer, fuller tails). Minus makes it shorter and tighter. 0 leaves it alone. Double-click for 0.
Band 1: Speed of the two level followers that tell the hit from the tail. Fast suits short clicks and hats, Medium suits most things, Slow suits long bass and pads.
Band 1: Threshold. Below this level the shaper does nothing, so quiet noise is not boosted. Drag the white slider on the level meter. Double-click it for -48.
Band 1: Max gain: the most this band can be turned up or down by the shaper, in dB (0 to 48, default 12). Keeps strong settings from running away.
Band 1: Output gain in dB, after the shaper and before the bands are added together. Double-click for 0.
Band 1: Mix: shaped band against the untouched band (aligned in time). 100% is fully shaped.
Display: scope or gain history.
Zoom the time axis of the display, 1x to 8x.
